result.summary: Keypath Repairs (Edrin Moss) says on the phone that the window-lock work was done on 19 Sept. Nothing on file backs this up. On 17 Sept Edrin said he had not collected the management keys and could not find the tenant at home. There is also no visit record and no invoice. I've asked the tenant to confirm whether anyone came and whether the locks and keys now work, and asked about the bathroom mould. I've asked Keypath to send its invoice with the visit date, how they got in, what was done to each window and how many keys were supplied. The ticket is on hold until 27 Sept. No invoice goes to the landlord until both replies are in and they match.
result.situation: The tenant reported faulty window sash locks and missing keys at Unit 2, 18 Brindlewick Mews. On 4 Sept the landlord said we could use the agency's own provider, with no cost limit (event 003). Hearthline Access was swapped for Keypath Repairs. Keypath never confirmed a visit time. On 17 Sept they said they had tried three times without keys. Since then they have said on the phone that the work was done on 19 Sept (events 023/025) and promised an invoice on 25 Sept. Nothing confirms the work, and no invoice has arrived. The tenant also mentioned bathroom mould on 9 Sept, and nothing has been done about it. The CRM still shows stage 'intake'.

judgement.why_this_decision: The only evidence the work was done is Edrin's word (events 023/025). It conflicts with his 17 Sept statement (event 022): no keys collected, tenant out at work. The tenant can settle this quickly, so I asked them rather than escalating. Paying or forwarding an invoice would need proof the work was done and a check of the amount, especially as the landlord set no cost limit (event 003). So the right move is to get both sides' accounts and hold the ticket with a follow-up date. classify_reply suggested human review (needs_human_response 0.72, dissatisfied 0.45). That fits holding off on closing, not escalating straight away. recall_lessons returned no lessons to follow.

alternatives_considered.option: Accept the completion claim and move to close-out
alternatives_considered.why_not: Nothing on file shows a visit, and the claim contradicts event 022. That breaks the rule against treating work as done without confirmation.
The tenant and contractor can answer the open questions. Escalating now would stall a routine job. If the replies conflict or the invoice doesn't match, I'll escalate.

alternatives_considered.option: Ask the landlord for approval again so the CRM stage can move
alternatives_considered.why_not: The landlord already approved by email (event 003). Asking again would be noise. I recorded the approval as a profile fact instead.

checks_performed: Approvals: the landlord approved by email (event 003) with no cost limit or scope. There is no approval record in the CRM, so moving to scheduling was refused.
Contractor: Hearthline Access was stood down (event 012) and Keypath Repairs instructed (event 018).
Dates and access: Keypath said on 17 Sept they had no keys and no access, then claimed the work was done on 19 Sept. The two statements conflict.
Invoice: none on file and no attachments, so there is no amount to check.
Safety: the tenant reported bathroom mould (event 006). There are no emergency signs. A bedroom sash that won't lock is a security issue to keep an eye on.
assumptions: The landlord's 'proceed' in event 003 covers inspection and repair of the sash locks and keys, but not an open-ended amount.

next_follow_up.what: Chase the tenant for confirmation and Keypath for the invoice and visit details. Then check the invoice against the work described. If it is all confirmed and matches, pass the invoice to the landlord and move to close-out. If not, escalate. Raise the bathroom mould as its own job.
